proposed_rules.trigger: A text node at the very top of the tree (rc1) whose content is a raw JS boot snippet, e.g. starting with document.addEventListener("DOM...
proposed_rules.decision: Exclude entirely from block inventory; source-leak artifact analogous to leaked-css-text-node but for JS.
proposed_rules.rationale: Recurs identically at rc1 on every captured page in this batch; boilerplate script text rendered visibly due to a source bug, never content.

proposed_rules.trigger: A [region] node containing FAQ answer text appears a second time as a sibling outside the main content flow (after the footer), duplicating text already nested under an accordion item.
proposed_rules.decision: Treat as a duplicate of the nested accordion answer already captured in the FAQ block; do not add as separate content.
proposed_rules.rationale: The page-tree capture promotes elements rendered outside their DOM parent (absolutely-positioned accordion panels), duplicating content already represented.

provenance.evidence: C185 rc4 duplicates rc2c9c3 answer text

proposed_rules.trigger: A trailing rc3 zone with fixed text 'The best no-code platform for...' plus a pipe-separated link row, identical across pages.
proposed_rules.decision: Model as a sitewide footer fragment, not page content; exclude from per-page block inventory.
proposed_rules.rationale: Identical structure/text recurs at the same position on every page in this batch, indicating global template chrome.

proposed_rules.trigger: A page-6 comparison template repeats the pattern 'competitor name label + list of [3x1] rows' twice in succession (rc2c3: detailed prose reasons, rc2c4: short feature-snapshot lines) before a third, richer alternating-background comparison zone (rc2c5).
proposed_rules.decision: Model both rc2c3 and rc2c4 as two instances of the same reusable comparison-table block type (differing only in row content/length), rather than inventing two distinct block types or merging them into one multi-column block. Rejected alternatives: (a) two distinct block types ('comparison-reasons' and 'comparison-snapshot'), (b) merge rc2c3+rc2c4 into a single wide comparison block spanning both zones.
proposed_rules.rationale: Both zones share the same shape (a competitor-name row followed by N one-line/one-paragraph rows) and only differ in content verbosity, matching the variant-is-css-not-new-block philosophy extended to block reuse rather than a new type per instance.

provenance.evidence: C185 rc2c3c1 vs rc2c4c2 both competitor-label + [3x1] row lists
